text:
Alex: Quick follow-up from the RFC review — want to kick off a small spike to validate service ownership curation ideas. TL;DR: can we carve the runtime's tenant-routing surface into a thin 'route-decision' service and a stateful 'session-core' without adding N+1 network hops?
Maria: +1. we need concrete perf numbers though. any ideas on what to prototype?
Jamal: I'd prototype a colocated proxy approach first: keep route-decision as GRPC, co-locate with request ingress to avoid extra cross-datacenter hops. measure p99 and CPU overhead.
Sara: agree with Jamal. also want to capture where KV cache ownership lands. if session-core owns KV, route-decision must carry cache keys in header.
Tim: flagged a tradeoff: if route-decision grows richer (model affinity, billing tags) it becomes a hot path. maybe push heavy policy evaluation to an async enrichment step.
Alex: good point. spike should include: 1) colocated GRPC route-decision prototype, 2) session-core owning per-session KV, 3) a fallback where route-decision includes enriched headers. compare latency and op counts.
Maria: rough benchmarks requested: baseline p50/p95/p99, CPU per-req, and token throughput delta. 1k requests/s with synthetic traces should be ok.
Jamal: I'll sketch the prototype today. pseudo-config I plan to use:
```
service route-decision {
  transport: grpc
  colocate_with: ingress
  responsibilities: [ "tenant_routing", "model_affinity_hint" ]
}
service session-core {
  transport: http2
  responsibilities: [ "kv_ownership", "session_state", "kv_cache" ]
}
```
Sara: will this require schema tweaks to cookies/headers? we need a stable header contract and versioning plan.
Tim: header contract + versioned proto is fine. add a 'route-v' header and a small compatibility matrix.
Alex: infra-bot can we get a quick perf job queued for the spike harness? tag it 'svc-curation-spike'
infra-bot: Job queued: infra/perf/svc-curation-spike. Build 2026-03-20_02. You will get results in ~45m.
Maria: for the tech-debt paydown piece — can we also run a static dependency scan to see which modules would be affected by moving KV ownership? I suspect 3 cross-cutting packages.
Jamal: noted. I'll add a change-impact checklist: owners, deps, runtime hooks, migration steps.
Sara: migration idea: shadow-write to session-core for 2 weeks, enable read-after-write gradually. this reduces cutover risk.
Tim: fallback policy: if session-core is unavailable, route-decision should fallback to legacy sync path. define SLOs for cutover window.
Alex: timeline proposal: 2-week spike, perf results + dependency map => decision doc. if green, 6-week incremental extraction with weekly rollouts.
Maria: sounds reasonable. can we add a quick eval on cost delta? dedicated calls might increase egress/compute. metric: $/token delta estimated.
Jamal: will include rough cost model in the spike deliverable.
Sara: UX for developers: a single SDK surface should remain. internal split must be invisible to app teams. add that to constraints.
Tim: adding constraint: no change to public API, must support feature flags for gradual opt-in.
Alex: ok folks — volunteers? Jamal for prototype, Maria for perf/metrics, Sara for schema and migration plan, Tim for SLOs and rollout playbook. I'll author the decision doc after results.
Maria: I'll monitor infra job and post results.
infra-bot: Perf job completed: p50 +3ms, p95 +18ms, p99 +42ms for colocated route-decision; CPU +6%. full results uploaded: https://perf.internal/reports/svc-curation-spike/2123456789
Alex: preliminary looks promising. Maria, can you pull the perf summary into the doc and schedule a 30-min sync for next Tue?
Maria: done — scheduled Tue 10:00. agenda: review perf, deps, migration playbook. :calendar:
Jamal: I'll post the prototype repo link in the thread later.
Sara: thanks all — this feels like the right balance between modularization and preserving runtime economics. :thumbsup:
